text: I will highlight two, where I was involved, was covering the duties of CIO 1 Tanglin Police Division.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The first case involved a rape case, of an 11-year-old girl who was going for tuition in the day.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She was raped at a staircase landing of a flat.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was a terribly trying moment for her.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But amazingly, she was able to provide a good description of the assailant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We devoted full attention to the case, leaving no stones unturned.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I still remember the note from the girl's father who expressed his appreciation over the work that we did.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He said that the apprehension and conviction of the assailant brought closure which allowed him and his daughter to move on.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: His daughter would be about 36 or 37 years old now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Member Ms Sylvia Lim shared her experience of a rape victim who unfortunately was not told the reasons why the AGC did not proceed with her complaint and charge the accused in Court.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But she would certainly agree with me that between the time when we were in the Police force and now, great strides have been taken to improve the process.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have not arrived yet, but we have made great progress.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The second case I will never forget involved my colleague, the late SI Boo Tiang Huat.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He was the OC of Whitley NPP, if I remember correctly.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: At that time, there was a spate of housebreaking at homes under the charge of the NPP.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He personally led anti-house breaking rounds, night after night, to deter such incidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He felt it his personal responsibility to lead these efforts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Personally, for myself and colleagues who attended the scene, it was tough to accept that a colleague we saw earlier in the morning has sacrificed his life in the course of duty.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was tougher for his wife and his young children, whom I accompanied to the scene to pray for SI Boo's soul later that day.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Police officers, past and present have spilled blood, sweat and tears in their mission to ensure the safety and security of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng and Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How and several other hon Members have storied careers in the Police force They know this for a fact.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The core values of the Singapore Police officers are courage, even if it means to risk their lives, loyalty, integrity and fairness.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On fairness, SPF's published credo is as follows and I quote,"We are fair in our dealings with people, irrespective of race, religion, gender, age, standing in life and irrespective of whether they are victims, suspects or convicts."  This is this unstinting devotion to duty that allowed Singapore to achieve the enviable reputation of being a relatively safe country with low crime rate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That is not to say there is no discipline cases within the force.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Yes, from time to time, we have black sheep.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These persons will be dealt with effectively by SPF, CPIB and the Courts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But their conduct is not representative of the vast majority of upright, dedicated and hardworking Police officers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And earlier today, we heard Minister Shanmugam saying, maybe even overworked Police officers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I continued to be involved in criminal and pro bono work.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As a pro bono lawyer, I have acted for vulnerable and disadvantaged people.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In fact, this eventually led me to politics.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I highlight two cases where I was involved in.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My very first trial was a pro bono case to defend a young man accused of shoplifting.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He and his family had very modest means and could not pay for a lawyer.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He had walked out of the department store with items that he did not pay for.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Luckily for him, the Court was persuaded that he walked out of the store accidentally and acquitted him.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Recently, I took on a Court-assigned pro bono case involving a mentally disordered person with little education.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: His father had passed away and his mother was a cleaner at a hawker centre.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He was accused of stealing coins from a vending machine.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I was exploring a community sentence, a Mandatory Treatment Order, to be imposed on him even though his prognosis for recovery was not good.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As it turned out, he subsequently assaulted his own mother.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That put paid to my efforts and he was sentenced to prison for his offences.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Anil Balchandani, the lawyer who acted for Ms Parti Liyani, is a good example of a selfless legal professional devoted to the cause of justice on behalf of persons who ordinarily would not be able to afford to pay for the services of a lawyer.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am confident that many more lawyers would be motivated by his example.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This can only auger well for our country.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also wish to state that I have acted for people who have occupied important positions and have been charged in Court for various criminal offences.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For example, I acted for Mr Choo Wee Khiang, a former Member of Parliament and Mr Chuang Shaw Peng, a former Nominated Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In none of the cases that I dealt with, for the vulnerable persons and the "connected" persons, if I could use that word, did I get the feeling that the justice system was tilted in favour of "connected" persons, as compared to the persons who are disadvantaged.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Judge deciding whether to grant bail or allowing the person to be released on his own cognisance, would be something that has to be dealt with after considering the offence that the person is charged for, the kind of sentence that may be imposed and, of course, the strong presumption of innocence until proven guilty.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And I have seen Judges deciding to allow persons of humble means to be let off, to be bailed or rather, to be released on a personal bond.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Judge would have to decide in the circumstances of the case, whether a fine is an adequate punishment.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And there are other options as well, particularly in the last few years, we have, as some Members have pointed out, the community aentence option in addition to the usual options.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, there is a discretion given to the Judge to make sure that the ends of justice, not just from the perspective of the accused, but from the perspective of the victim and the state, are met.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There have also been great strides in improving the criminal justice system.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would not go through ground that has already been highlighted by hon Members who spoke before me.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would just go straight to the fact that clearly, there is broad agreement between Members from both sides of the House about the importance of fairness, access and independence being the cornerstones of Singapore's justice system from inception and recognition that there has been continuous efforts to improve the justice system to build a fair and just society, regardless of one's personal background, race, religion or social economic background.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With that in mind, Mr Speaker, Sir, I seek your permission to move an amendment to the Motion under discussion to reflect this broad agreement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do you have a copy of the amendment?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: May copies be distributed to hon Members, please.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: With your leave, Sir, I would like to explain the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Murali, can you pause for a while.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Leader, would you like to suspend the Standing Orders for the extension of time for Mr Murali?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: With that, let me now go through the amendments.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is to leave this Motion in broad terms so that at the end of the day, it is an affirmation that the Government would continue to remedy any shortcoming that is brought up, and to allow the conversation to happen in this House about what further steps need to be taken.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: At the end of the day, the buck stops with this House.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is this House that has to make the political decisions to pass legislation, to move amendments to the Constitution in relation to the justice system.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, the buck must stop here and this Motion reflects that reality.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I do not think anything is taken away with the amendments that I propose.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The raison d'etre of the PAP is to build a fair and just society, founded on justice and equality for all people, especially the disadvantaged.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Just a few days ago, Miss Lim, a daughter of a man who was on his deathbed approached me.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: She was served with a Stay-Home Notice or SHN, and she was extremely concerned that she would not be able to see her father at the deathbed because she had to serve the SHN.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Within three hours, she was able to see her father in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Which other country would be able to do this and this was way after office hours?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is not the time to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And I believe my hon friends from Workers' Party across the aisle would also hold true to the same values.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are five amendments proposed by Mr Murali Pillai.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: These are: "(1) In line 1, to delete 'affirms' and insert 'recognises'; (2) In line 3, to delete 'calls on the Government to recognise' and insert 'affirms the Government's continuous efforts since Independence to build a fair and just society'; (3) In line 3, to delete 'its shortcomings' and insert 'any shortcoming'; (4) In line 4, after the words 'regardless of' to insert the words 'race, language, religion, economic'; (5) In line 5, to delete 'including facilitating a review of the justice system' and insert a full-stop." Does any Member wish to speak on these five amendments?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And, if so, Members wishing to speak on these five amendments can speak on them en bloc.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will now deal with the five amendments proposed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For those who are dissenting, if I can request that you raise your hands, so that we can record it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The original Motion, as amended, is now before the House.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Am I not given the right of reply?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: After Ms Indranee Rajah, you will wrap up.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Or are you asking to speak on the vote on the Motion, as amended?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Yes, you will be rounding up the debate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She also said that today's Motion is not about tearing down the system or discouraging those who work in law enforcement, the AGC or the Courts; far from it, it is about a desire to raise the system to the next level, which indeed I think is something that we can all agree on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Workers' Party had put forward some suggestions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would like in my speech to address the suggestions that were put forward by Mr Pritam Singh, the Leader of the Opposition, specifically with regard to decoupling the function of the Attorney-General and the function of the Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But actually, the second two points are really premised on the first.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, let me deal with the first one.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the first, he takes charge of three areas – legislation, international affairs and civil matters.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the second, as the Public Prosecutor, he has to prosecute without fear or favour.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The essence of Mr Singh's argument is that there is a conflict, an inherent conflict in these two roles.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And he articulated it in this form, that as the Government's legal advisor, the Attorney-General's duty is to protect the interests of the Government and as the Public Prosecutor, it is to represent the public and prosecute without fear or favour.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addressing this, he also mentioned that Ms Sylvia Lim had raised this point previously.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Indeed, she had, but not quite in the same way.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what I want to do is firstly, address how Ms Sylvia Lim articulated it and then, I will go on to address how Mr Singh articulated it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To be fair, they both want to reach the same point, which is that there is a conflict so you should decouple them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But actually, the argument has evolved a little bit.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She put it in this way: "in order to further strengthen the system and shore up the independence of the Public Prosecutor", we should "consider splitting the two roles...to reside in two different offices, so that the person who is the Public Prosecutor or PP, is not the same person taking the Government's instructions in non-criminal matters.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is no issue with the same person in both roles because the system ensures that in his PP role, the AG acts independently.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the thrust of that argument that Ms Sylvia Lim originally made was that, you are taking the Government's instructions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You take the Government's instructions on the civil matters, on the other matters, but not when it comes to the decision to prosecute.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In responding to that, then Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong also pointed out that the reason why the role is separate in other countries is because in those countries where the roles are separate – in countries such as UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand – the Attorney-General holds political office.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He is a political office holder or he sits in Cabinet.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is therefore the question of being subject to political pressures and the separation of the role of the Attorney-General from the public prosecutor in those jurisdictions has to be looked at in that context because he is subject to political pressure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Whereas here – and I will go on to discuss that in a bit more detail later – our situation is different because our Constitution has safeguards in that our AG does not hold political office.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The constitutional safeguards ensure that he is protected from such political pressures, and it allows him to discharge both his roles as PP and the Government's legal advisor without fear or favour.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I come back to Mr Singh's argument today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Previously, the argument was you should do it the same way as other countries because of independence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then, of course, it was pointed out that in other countries, because the AG is a political office holder, that is why you have to separate it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, today, the argument is that as the Government's legal advisor, the AG's duty is to protect the interests of the Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because as Mr Singh pointed out, as the Government's legal advisor, the AG takes charge of legislation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when he protects the Government's interest in legislation, that has nothing to do with his prosecutorial function.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: His other role as advisor is international affairs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When he is advising the Government on international affairs, that has nothing to do with prosecution.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When he is advising the Government on civil matters, that has nothing to do with his role as a prosecutor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And when it comes to his role as a prosecutor, we agree he must be able to prosecute without fear or favour – and he does.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The track record shows that the Attorney-General has prosecuted high level people before, without fear or favour.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This includes, for example, the prosecution of Mr Ng Boon Gay, the former director of the CNB; the prosecution of Mr Peter Lim, the former SCDF Commissioner; and more recently, the charges against Mr Pek Lian Guan, CEO and Executive Director of Tiong Seng Holdings, and Pay Teow Heng, Director of Tiong Seng Contractors (Private) Limited.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there has never been an issue about being able to act independently.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh then raised a couple of examples of where there may be such conflict.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And he talked about the difficulty the AG may have in prosecuting Government-linked companies, for example.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But again, that is not the case because we have had no difficulty doing that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have had no issue with prosecuting anybody, whether Government-linked or not, provided the PP sees that there is a case on the face of it to bring charges.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, Mr Singh went on to say that it would be difficult, for example, if in the case of – it is a hypothetical example, not a current one – a future government, where the Prime Minister and the AG may be very chummy and therefore the Attorney-General or the PP may not wish to bring a prosecution, either against the Prime Minister if there was an offence committed or somebody close, that thereby, he may have a desire to keep his job for favours or simply because the hypothetical alleged future Prime Minister and the AG are cronies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And it envisages that if such a situation may happen where the Prime Minister does not act in accordance with his duty, there is a check, there is a balance, and there is an avenue where corruption and other offences can be prosecuted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, really, I have dealt with the alleged conflict.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the position is that there is no conflict between the two roles, for the reasons I have explained.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh did point out that in other countries and he named two.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He did not name them, but we know who they are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He said that in both these countries that prominent cases of the Attorney-General being subject to political pressure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our system protects the Attorney-General from being subject to political pressure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The AG is appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the Prime Minister cannot do it just as a whim.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is very difficult under our system to remove the Attorney-General.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Removal is by the President and this time not acting on advice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is by the President, acting in his or her discretion, and if it concurs with the advice of the Prime Minister, and the Prime Minister cannot tender such advice except if the AG is unable to discharge the functions of his office whether arising from infirmity of body or mind or any other cause or for misbehaviour.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: [Please refer to "Clarification by Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development", Official Report, 4 November 2020, Vol 95, Issue No 13, Correction by Written Statement section.] So, the Prime Minister cannot just say, "I advise you to get rid of the AG because I happen not to like the way he did this prosecution, or I wanted him to do this and he did not do it".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Prime Minister is constrained by the constitutional provisions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And further, the Prime Minister cannot tender such advice without the concurrence of a tribunal, consisting of the Chief Justice and two other Judges of the Supreme Court.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, our system has safeguards to ensure the independence of the Attorney-General and this is very different from other jurisdictions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, in the US, for example, the Attorney-General's position is entirely at the President's pleasure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it is not so much about the appointment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is about whether or not once that person is in place, how easy is it for you to remove him.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And in our case, it is not easy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that gives the Attorney-General and the Public Prosecutor the assurance of knowing that he can carry out his duty without interference.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh then went on to say he had two suggestions for improvements, but the improvements are premised on being able to make out that there is a case that there was a conflict.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I have addressed why there is no conflict.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But there is one point I want to address, which is security of tenure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because I think the point that Mr Singh will likely make is that, well, you have all these safeguards, but if you have a relatively short term of tenure, then that sort of takes away from the ability to be independent.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But actually, that is not the case either.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some countries have a fixed tenure for their Attorneys-General, and some do not.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Officers in charge of prosecutions in England and Wales, Australia, New Zealand and Hong Kong have no security of tenure and typically serve predetermined terms which may be renewable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And in the US, there is no security of tenure at all.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the words of one of their former Attorney-Generals who was asked to resign, he said, "I serve at the pleasure of the President.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I've understood that from the day I took the job".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what is more important is the constitutional safeguards against removal, and those we have in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And he did say that such an individual can be considered for the role of Government legal advisor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That too is a little bit different from the position advanced by Ms Sylvia Lim before.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But shifted slightly – now, it has just become only Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Even if the Public Prosecutor who was previously an MP does his or her sincere best to be objective, they cannot help but be a product of their previous beliefs, which they perhaps still hold.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As a Public Prosecutor who was an MP of a political party and steeped in the party's ideology for years, he is likely to hold certain beliefs and approach things in certain ways.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the face of it, yes, it sounds a little bit worrying.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But let us ask ourselves, what does that actually mean?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What are the political views of the party that Mr Hri Kumar used to be in, for example.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Well, one of the views is we believe in meritocracy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As a member of the PAP, we believe in meritocracy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We believe in not having a corrupt system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not sure how this would affect his prosecutorial functions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also believe in a green and sustainable Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not sure how that would affect his prosecutorial functions as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I mean, what is it about the beliefs of the PAP that would somehow affect his prosecutorial functions?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is nothing in there that would conflict with the ability of the Deputy Attorney-General to prosecute cases.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the argument is being made that he may have a conflict because of a political reason, would he have to charge somebody who, for example, was from the party previously whom he knows, that is a different argument.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is basically a situation where you see a conflict of interest in which case, the right thing, the proper thing to do is you recuse yourself.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Which is exactly the approach that has been taken all along.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Minister Shanmugam explained, the earlier part of the prosecution, Mr Wong had nothing to do with it at all.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That was dealt with at a different level.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And since the matter has surfaced, he has recused himself very properly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the point I am making is that this is how the system works and that is the assurance that people can have, that if there is some conflict, that the Deputy Attorney-General or the Attorney-General will do the correct thing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I believe, Mr Speaker, I have addressed the points raised by Mr Singh.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I just would conclude by saying that it seems that there is much in common.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are some differences in terms of the approach towards the Motion which Mr Murali's amendment addresses.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I still take the view that the conflict is possible and that is the basis of the suggestion that I put in my speech.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I gave two examples: one was with regard to that Government-linked company, which I hypothesised.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Now, let me try and take it to some specifics.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There is an old article, 23 December 1997.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is an opinion piece by an individual who would later become the Attorney-General in Singapore, Mr Walter Woon.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And he talked about malfeasance, a corruption scandal involving Keppel again, but not the latest deferred prosecution agreement that was entered into by —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Singh, you are raising a point of clarification?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Not the deferred prosecution agreement between Brazil, the US and Singapore, but a similar scandal that occurred previously.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And there, what Mr Woon really says is the Attorney-General decides to go after the company, but then does not prosecute the individuals.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And so, the situation is the company can accept the fine, but the individuals who later may benefit because of these bribes that were given – they benefit through the fact that the company will give out more bonuses to them, for example.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, the question, of course, is do we have a situation where we can tell ourselves, "Look, there is no prospect, no implicit bias here".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is there a system we can consider of conceive of, which can reduce that prospect in the public perception?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And this is where I feel a division of the roles actually may be more helpful to the Government.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second point is with regard to security of tenure.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, a longer term for the Attorney-General I think would be good for the system.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The third point is about a Member of Parliament who takes on the role of AG.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Of course, I can agree with the Leader about integrity, meritocracy and so forth.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And that is a view that reasonable people can have a different view about.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: To that end, I did consider whether this position is supposed to be for all time.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Let us say, if an MP steps down in 2020, does it mean that he cannot take on the appointment as AG forever and ever?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Could there be some scope to consider at least a moratorium period or a garden leave period?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, if there is a question of some concession or some coming together as the Leader suggested in her wrapping-up paragraph and that the positions between the Government and Opposition are not so far apart, perhaps the Government can consider some of the proposals in that light to see how we can end up with a better legal system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But rather, it was a case where the Public Prosecutor was facing challenges in terms of getting the evidence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Attorney-General's office or the Public Prosecutor's office has requested further information and it is still pending.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second point was with respect to the term.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not sure if I got the point correctly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Just to extend the timing maybe to a longer period.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is what guarantees the independence of the system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The third point, how the public perceives it if somebody who was a former politician becomes a Public Prosecutor, the answer is has that person given anyone any cause for concern?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the person has resigned from the political party, the person takes on the duties, knows the duties and has not given any cause for concern or acted in any way, then there is no reason why the public should feel alarmed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But and this is a big "but", if that person in any way shows that he or she is not acting in accordance with the duties, then appropriate action would have to be taken.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is how we can make sure that our system remains independent, remains strong and remains robust.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I welcome the debate because I understand what drives it, which is the desire to improve the system and to make one better for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the first point, this is just as a matter of clarification with the Leader.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do not mean to be argumentative, but I am not referring to the latest Keppel infraction.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Keppel pleaded guilty, which meant that it admitted to the statement of facts without qualification", "the district judge fined Keppel the maximum $100,000 on each of the charges and a total of $300,000, and that was the end of the matter".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I think the point that is being made in this particular case is, the question on the minds of the public in the context of a public prosecutor that also performs the role of the Government legal advisor is, was that discretion, the prosecutorial discretion exercised appropriately?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I think this is where as the Leader suggests, she understands where the thrust of some of our concerns are coming from.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: These are the sort of situations which we feel may compromise in the public eye, rightly or wrongly, the independence of the AG.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the point is that there does not seem to be anything in what Mr Singh has said which indicates why further action was not taken.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We do not know at this point of time and I do not wish to speculate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The point I wish to make is that it is not at all clear that that has anything to do with the fact that the PP also has an AG role.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think where the Leader of the Opposition is coming from is that whatever the case in the prosecution, people must feel satisfied that the prosecutor in exercising his functions and duties, has done so properly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I have given an example of how not in 1997 but many years down the line, where it is a case of the company and potential liability for individuals, company was pursued and the case against individuals is still open.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you can see that whatever it is, the Public Prosecutor looks at it and where it is appropriate, takes the necessary action.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Everyone who has spoken accepts that fairness, access and independence are cornerstones of our justice system.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The unfairness faced by the poor was highlighted by MP for Sengkang Ms He Ting Ru and myself.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We have described how a lack of resources can unfairly impact households who are faced with charges for offences, even minor ones.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This is a major societal issue that if unaddressed could worsen the class divide and entrench inter-generational poverty.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We have made suggestions on how the unfairness may be mitigated such as re-looking at composition fines and bail.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Fairness is also an issue for those not comfortable in the English language, when it comes to statement recording by law enforcement.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For this, I have suggested recording statements documented in other languages.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Ms He raised the unfairness faced by those who are wrongly accused and suffered damage and harm.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: She argued that there should be recourse to compensation, balanced with the need for effective law enforcement in prosecutions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As for crime victims, I have highlighted that their role and rights need strengthening, if the system is to be fairer to them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As far as access to justice is concerned, Ms He and Mr Gerald Giam, MP for Aljunied, have acknowledged the existence of legal aid schemes but pointed out that enhancements are due.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Mr Giam has particularly highlighted the disadvantages faced by migrant workers, whether it is crime victims or accused persons.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On the right to consult a lawyer when arrested, Ms He pointed out that this was a constitutional right and a review is needed to ascertain if it is functioning optimally, balancing the interests of law enforcement and the accused.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As regard to the third cornerstone of independence, several of my Party colleagues touched on this.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also asked if the criteria for the appointment of State Court Judges should be raised to a higher threshold of seniority.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also proposed a longer contractual period of five years for appointees to the post of AG and that any future nominee should have experience in criminal practice either as a judge, prosecutor or defence counsel.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Another Aljuined MP Mr Leon Perera raised the need for additional independent checks on the actions of public bodies through the office of an ombudsman.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have also suggested that it is prudent to do a review on whether there is any institutional sub-culture that inadvertently results in discriminatory outcomes between the rich and poor.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If such a sub-culture exists, steps should be taken to eradicate it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan praised our criminal justice system and said we should not tar everyone with the same brush.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: His point was that we should not be critical of all who work in the criminal justice system.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And, of course, that was not my intention, as I pointed out that there are many public-spirited professionals in law enforcement, prosecution and the Courts, who take their mission seriously.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Mr Vikram Nair supported the spirit behind my Motion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He agreed with the principle of criminal law reform and spoke of the reforms legislated in the CPC in 2010.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also said that there could be greater access to counsel by accused persons at an earlier stage and he agreed with the idea of a public defender's office.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He said that my points on the plight of the poor, improvement of processes of law enforcement agencies and support of crime victims were things that could be looked into.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I also think Mr Leong Mun Wai for supporting the original Motion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam reiterated points made by Minister Shanmugam in his Statement on Ms Parti Liyani's case.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: She said that unfairness is not pervasive and that processes and channels for help exist in our system.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: However, she agreed that our systems are not perfect and that we should work on our shortcomings and remedy them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If not, we were planting the seeds of doubt and eroding trust in the system.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Mr Louis Ng raised concerns about the timeline to implement video recording and on translation of statements.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Mr Murali Pillai gave us a lecture on the separation of government powers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also shared his experiences working within the system.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As for government responses, I am glad that Minister Shanmugam has recognised several issues that we have raised.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He said that on many issues, we were on the same page, pushing at an open door.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He said we were setting out positions of principle and he did not object to them, but that the front bench needed to think about the implementation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He said that on a few points, things are already moving.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On legal aid for the poor, the Minister agreed with the principle, but felt that we should proceed cautiously in view of the experience in other countries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We welcome that action is being taken on the above matters.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For instance, he said that as far as recording of statements is concerned, audio-visual recordings are the gold standard but resource issues were a bottleneck.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On compensation for miscarriages of justice, the Minister felt that only vexatious cases deserved compensation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We ask the Government keep an open mind on this, as there could be other cases deserving of compensation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Minister Edwin Tong talked about the ombudsman and rejected our suggestion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He pointed out that the Government was more concerned with overall outcomes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Minister of State Gan Siow Huang highlighted the efforts made by the Government to support migrant workers in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: They have shared with us their own experiences of being crime victims or suspects or having family members being subject to such experiences.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Questions raised by the public include the following: where is the justice when someone is wrongly accused and had to endure humiliation in investigations, only to be acquitted?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Does the prosecution aim to win cases at all costs?
